audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows contradicted their own why. win[0] said Lillia while whys[0] says neither can commit; win[1] said Skill while whys[1] describes her poking freely; win[3] said K'Sante while whys[3] ends 'so it stays a coin-flip'; win[5] and win[6] said K'Sante while whys[5]/whys[6] describe her first AP item and full-build kiting reclaiming the game.
audit.why: 43.22% over 715 games. The packet chart (Skill, Lillia, K'Sante, Skill, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia) matches the prose exactly — only the tokens were wrong.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 3, 5 and 6 set to Skill, Lillia, Skill, Lillia, Lillia in phases[].side and win[] together, with ratings re-scaled to 5/3/5/3/2.

audit.whatIsWrong: Blooming Blows was described only as 'her kite + move speed stacks' with no cooldown, and Lilting Lullaby had no number, so 'commit when it is down' was unactionable.
audit.why: Blooming Blows is 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s — effectively always up, which is why the level-3 window is the only one. Lilting Lullaby is 150/130/110s.
audit.corrected: 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s written into the interactions row and dosFull[0].d, and the 450 Q range gap named in whys[3] and wants.foe[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Four errors. (1) 'Q3 knockup' in five paths — Ntofo Strikes has no knockup or third cast; at 2 stacks it fires a shockwave that pulls. (2) 'her W bounce' / 'bait out her W/E mobility' — Watch Out! Eep! is stationary area damage and Swirlseed is a rolling projectile; NEITHER is mobility. Her move speed comes from Blooming Blows (Q). Telling a reader to bait her W for her mobility gets them killed holding a cooldown for a thing that does not exist. (3) 'All Out's range buff' — Riot's text gives All Out increased damage, healing and transformed abilities, not range. (4) Lillia repeatedly called 'him/his'.
audit.why: Kit text is the authority; range on All Out is not in the file, so it is unknown and must not be asserted.
audit.corrected: Pull named correctly everywhere, move speed reattributed to Blooming Blows, the range claim dropped for the duelist shift, and — the decisive addition — Blooming Blows' edge TRUE damage written in, since the whole page told the reader armour was merely 'ignored' rather than actively the wrong buy.

edits.before: Lillia has no hard CC and no escape until she ramps move speed, so level 1 is genuinely even — you both just farm. But the second she has W (Watch Out!) and E (Swirlseed) at level 2, she starts poking you with magic damage that your armor stacking does absolutely nothing against, and she dances just outside your short Q range. Don't chase a Q3 you can't land — she bounces away with W and your Q slow is too little to pin her. Your only clean window is level 3: bait her W, then W her into a wall for the extended stun and follow with Q3 knockup.
edits.after: Lillia has no hard CC and no escape until she ramps move speed, so level 1 is genuinely even — you both just farm. But the second she has W (Watch Out! Eep!) and E (Swirlseed) at level 2, she starts poking you with damage your armor stacking does absolutely nothing against, and she dances just outside your 450-range Q. Don't chase a pull you can't land — Blooming Blows keeps stacking her move speed and your Q slow is too little to pin her. Your only clean window is level 3: bait her W, then W her into a wall for the extended stun and follow with the two-stack Ntofo pull.

edits.before: You lose the long game outright. Full-AP Lillia is a perpetual-motion kiter — her passive DOT and stacked move speed outrun every dash you have, and your entire armor-stacking identity is dead weight against her magic damage. You can't peel what you can't touch, and All Out's range buff doesn't matter when she's never in front of you. Your only path is to have already snowballed off a level 3 all-in or a gank; if the game goes late even, she wins by attrition. Group, force objectives early, and let your team apply the lockdown you can't.
edits.after: You lose the long game outright. Full-AP Lillia is a perpetual-motion kiter — her max-health DOT passive and stacked move speed outrun every dash you have, and your armor-stacking identity is dead weight against magic damage that turns true on Q's edge. You can't peel what you can't touch, and All Out's duelist shift doesn't matter when she's never in front of you. Your only path is to have snowballed off a level 3 all-in or a gank; if the game goes late even, she wins by attrition. Group, force objectives early, and let your team apply the lockdown you can't.
